reviews.text:
My experience with Sonora Dental Group was extremely disappointing and ultimately led me to find a new dentist (Desert Sage Family Dental, which is nearby).

Over the course of being a patient (since 2018), I had multiple dental cleaning appointments canceled because the office did not have a hygienist available. Routine cleanings are basic preventive dental care, yet it seemed like scheduling was constantly unstable. It often felt like the office had more administrative days than actual patient-care days, which made it difficult to receive consistent dental care.

Communication and professionalism were also lacking. On one visit, I arrived for a minor dental procedure that had already been scheduled. I was brought back, fully numbed for the procedure, and then the dentist ultimately decided the procedure was not necessary and sent me home. Being numbed and prepared for treatment only to be told afterward that nothing would be done was frustrating and a clear example of poor communication and planning.

After dealing with these issues repeatedly, I decided to move my dental care to Desert Sage Family Dental, and the difference has been night and day. Their team is

Take it from a long time patient. I had been going for 5+ years . Ever since the office manager Devin left the place has fallen apart. Very unorganized, no empathy for people. Most of all trying to charge for additional work you don’t need . I just went to another brand new dental office and they said I didn’t need any of that work. Sonoran also tried to charge me for X-rays when I called up my insurance they said it’s covered . I almost paid the 200 dollars. They are not taking my money . When I said I was no longer going to use them the rep said “okay we will cancel your appt” not even a “what happened “ or “sorry” Please look elsewhere if you are in the process of finding a new dental office.

Terrible experience with Brenda and booking my appointment. I work out of town and don’t have access to my phone all the time. I made the appointment which should be good enough. When I spoke to her she was inconsiderate talking down and at me. To many other options, if you’re looking for a new dentist or are new to that area like me try someone else

this is the WORST office I have been to, Devin left. Had a scheduled appt with the oral surgeon last year which Sonora cancelled without my consent. I got screwed out of the rest of my benefits, been without bottom teeth for a year. I get a call 2 days ago that the oral surgeon is moving, her last day is in 2 days, looking at getting all top pulled and basically I’ll be without one plate. this is unbelievable. on the positive, DR. CHRIS IS AMAZING

I was told my insurance was approved and I would not owe anything. After my crown work was done while waiting on permanent crown, the office said my dental work was denied. Now I’m stuck without the permanent crown and the office not willing to fitting my crown until payment is made by me!!! Everything should have be approved before dental work began. Office staff was rude and unwilling to put in my crown, they’re holding me hostage until all the bill is paid.

Western Dental's website clearly states they accept Medicaid from Arizona's AHCCCS Medicaid program. They are also on the list that Mercy Care Medicaid provided. Then I get a call telling me they do not take Mercy Care Medicaid provided by Arizona AHCCCS. Zero stars!

Extremely dirty. Dust and debris everywhere. Dental floss on floor where I was being seen. Instruments dirty. Waited an hour for my appointment and then very rushed appointment with dentist. Would not go back.

this dentist sucks!! i went with extreme wisdom teeth and from the beginning the girl at front had an attitude, she told me she wouldn’t charge me for my appointment because the insurance offices were closed. then i waited 40 min to be taken back, my appointment being at 4, going back at 4:40. i got taken to a chair and waited 15 minutes more. when the dentist got there the chair ended up being broken, i got moved. the dentist then took one look at my mouth, seemed like a good person but didn’t really help me the way i needed help. i sat there again then the girl from the front brought in a long estimate of how much the extraction would cost AND sent me home. the worst part of i just got a bill for the visit. yes thats how bad it was!!

Been with this location for a while, definitely not the best experience. I first arrived with different name than what it is currently. I asked them to update the system since my insurance is under the new name. Not only was it not done but my insurance information has been incorrect the entire time and just recently got sorted. Name still has not been updated in their system and it’s causing issues for everyone. They are also refusing to give insurance my history for reviewing my case for said appeal. Not to mention it’s impossible to get anyone on the phone before the system disconnects the call, no voicemail option either.

tried going here, person i spoke with on the phone was the worse customer service person Ive spoken with in a while. couldn't verify any insurance info wanted me to call my insurance to see if they cover with them. Attitude was not friendly at all and just seemed like she wanted me to hang up, which I ended up doing.

About 2 years ago I did over 6 thousand dollars worth of work and decided to go here for a cleaning because the other place stopped taking my insurance. Arcadia modern dentistry told me that all the work I just got done needed to be REDONE and that it would cost me thousands on top of it. Got a $300 dollar cleaning from them and a second opinion somewhere else…. No work needs to be done and everything looks beautiful and healthy! Save yourself a headache and go somewhere else.

I came across Arcadia Modern Dentistry while searching for new patient cleaning/exam specials. Their website advertises a $59 new patient special, which includes a cleaning, comprehensive exam and X-rays. Shortly after scheduling online, I received a phone call from someone at their office asking for my insurance. I explained that I scheduled due to their advertised $59 new patient special; he replied that their website was outdated and it was no longer available. There’s no excuse for them not to have their website up-to-date, or to honor this offer since they still have it on their website. I would not give this business my business.

I would not recommend this practice. This practice is the stereotypical dental office that is only interested in making money. They will recommend unnecessary procedures and office visits, so they can bill your insurance. They had me coming in for teeth cleanings every 4 months and at each visit made it sound like my teeth were going to fall out even though I brush and floss twice daily and have overall healthy teeth. During one visit, the hygienist pulled up my insurance to confirm some unnecessary gum irrigation was covered. It was, so unsurprisingly, they did it. After doing 4 month office visits for over a year with no apparent improvement of my alleged issues according to them, I got a second opinion, which directly contradicted their recommended course of treatment. I encourage everyone to avoid going here.

Waste of time. I was explicit when I made appointment that I needed and expected a cleaning at time of appointment. They took x-rays, gave me a quote for work, and did not clean my teeth. I asked they not bill my insurance company as I did not get what I requested and will NEVER go back. They billed them anyway.

Went in for a cleaning. First time visiting so got X-rays which was fine. But then the Hygienist came in and not very personable at all. They immediately told me I needed a deep cleaning (my last cleaning was 8 months earlier at a different dentist who said my gums were fine). They then didn’t want to do the basic cleaning which was what I had scheduled with them. The dentist was nice enough and seemed professional, but then the hygienist came back in for the basic cleaning I insisted on and she was very rude. The cleaning seemed aggressive and rushed. At the end she said “so no fluoride?” I was very confused because I always thought that was just part of the basic cleaning. When I asked her why I wouldn’t get fluoride she said “that’s what I was told you said”. It had never been asked and hadn’t come up. When I told her exactly that she replied “well I don’t know!”. Felt like she was mad I didn’t agree to the deep cleaning right away. Plus she left the fluoride on my teeth and it left a sticky, gummy film in my mouth all day. Honestly it was just a weird, uncomfortable experience. Definitely will not be returning. Based on the other reviews it seems like the upsell is their normal
My experience here was not the best. I ended up getting a second opinion and found a better option.

What a very odd experience. Here is what happened: they call me 20minutes before my first exam appt. for 8am asking me to reschedule. I said I was already 5 minutes away, and she said to just come in and they will see me early. Arrive at 7:45. Wasn't seen until 8:20, but oh well. Not a big deal. We get my Xrays done and he says my teeth look good, just some plaque. He then asks me who my insurance is (odd question to be sure). After I tell him who my insurance carrier is, he decides to prod around my gums for 20 minutes. Out of left field, he decides the sky is falling and that I have gum disease and I need a $2500 operation to fix it. $500 out of pocket with my insurance. I said no thank you but I would like to schedule a cleaning, covered under my insurance. This guy proceeds to tell me he can't in good conscience schedule a cleaning, and that if he were to see me again that I had to do the operation. Truly mind blowing. Although, I shouldn't be surprised, as others in reviews have accused him of doing the same thing. I too will not pay for this guys boat (he will say he doesnt have one but its a funny anecdote). I've asked around, and nobody has ever heard of a dentist refusing

First to preface my comment- I am one of those individuals who had neglected my teeth. And for those of you who have always taken care of your teeth, the shame and guilt and feelings of a deep sense of dread tend to compound the issue further by a fear of showing up and being humiliated. During his examination, Dr. Milana reinforced this feeling by commenting on my upper right teeth saying, "And these are 'TOAST' ". While I'm not the most sophisticated person in the world, it doesn't take a rocket scientist (or evidently a dentist) to figure out that the word "TOAST" belongs in a culinary conversation about Denny's, not as a cold and completely insensitive comment from someone with 4.8 stars on Google. Knowledgeable and qualified yes, personable and compassionate.....well you be the judge.

As a follow-up, your "Toast" comment was followed directly by you saying that those teeth were TERMINAL. Again I ask you whether the word terminal belongs in a conversation about a patient's teeth or when giving directions to the airport. I just maybe I'm just a whiner....
Probably the worst dentist I have ever been to. Unprofessional, lacking in zero interpersonal relationship skills. Always felt he was trying to make boat payment. Please don’t go to this dentist

My family and I went to this office due to her having an issue with a tooth. This was my wife's first time going to the dentist. I picked this dentist due to the good reviews from online, however after she was called in for the exam, which I should have went in with her, she told me the dentist just poked on her gums without telling her what he was going to do and also picked at the bad tooth and caused her pain. After the exam was finished we were called into an office and was explained by the receptionist of what was to be done and what were the cost. I felt like we were in a used car lot and was being upsold for other services. We really only needed to have the one tooth to be pulled and nothing else. We were then referred to an oral surgeon since they stated that it could not be done there. We ended up leaving. About 15 minutes later, my wife was in terrible pain from the tooth that the dentist had picked. We were in late afternoon traffic and I had to get to a Walgreen's as soon as possible to pick up some excedrin for her. We will not be going back to this dentist!

I went to my appointment in June and they overcharged me on my copayment. When I asked why it was more they said they could not verify my insurance and that it takes two days to verify. I informed them that they had over a week because they took all my info when scheduling me. Then the office manager came out and was really short with me. She threatened me that I could possibly be charged up to $250 because they were not even taking my insurance. So I shut my mouth and paid the $80. I had scheduled the week before maybe two and I had asked before they even scheduled me if they accepted my dental plan. Their excuse was that they had a temp worker the day I was scheduled. They took my x-rays and did my initial checkup and took my money and never even followed up with me once. My insurance got charged for everything they did during that visit. Now I have to start all over and get charged again elsewhere. I wasn’t a new patient just a new insurance plan. It was just the front of house that made me feel like I did not belong there.

Would not recommend even though I was a patient for over 2 years. Staff and business manager have no accountability and threatened to cancel my surgery when they messed up and didn’t have my forms or medication in advance
The oral surgeon met with me once for 5 minutes or less and did not go over the procedure well or address my anxiety concerns with sedation.
I was very aware in the beginning of this surgery and received attitude from the surgeon and I know I was shaking profusely throughout the surgery and when my mom came to get me I was still shaking profusely and the “care” team did not seem concerned or willing to help.
This place does not care about their patients and see you only as a client with money
I explained that I was transportation for a patient, I asked to use the restroom. The person at the front desk told me the restroom was for patients only

This place was pretty good until they convinced me to get a procedure that they assured me was covered by my insurance, then started trying to bill me for it 6 months later, and then sent it to collections.
My mom went for a dental cleaning. They told her she had on infection and they lie about the diagnosis. They just wanted to take advantage of her and she didn’t even get her teeth clean.

I cannot say enough terrible things about this place. Diana, the office manager, left me feeling as though she though I was garbage because that is how she treated me. The dentist? Incredibly incompetent not only at dentistry, but lacking any sort of bedside manner or business sense. This dental group epitomizes why people both hate dentists and do not trust them! I'll never go back!
Amazing hygienist, but shady billing practices and condescending office manager. Do not recommend.

Called twice to ask for cash price and to confirm my appt. When I got there they said I needed more and it would be more than double the cost. I flew there for a 7 am appt across town. Very disappointed. There was no responsibility for giving me bad information over the phone twice. Unfortunate because the first experience was great:/

Worst dentist in the Biltmore-arcadia neighborhood. Un-trained staff, horrible customer service, arrogant bedside manner, and a lack of empathy for patient. After 10 + years they have lost my business and all future referrals. Unfortunately I’ve referred almost 5 friends/family. Looks like we’re all moving to a new dentist.
Horrible experience. Excessively painful and poorly done fillings. Stains were not addressed during cleaning only offered upsell whitening. Glad I went somewhere else!

office was very unprofessional and unsanitary. the front desk lady was very rude and was dressed provocative. dr seemed like he was in a hurry and i did not feel comfortable at all. will not be back if i could give 0 stars i would.

I understand most people will look at the 4.9 rating and ignore this review. I urge you to highly consider the seriousness of what my review represents.

Years ago I went to Dr. Harman regularly (as regular as you might see a dentist). At a routine cleaning I was told I had a cavity and they could drill it and fill it. I declined and ignored it. 6 months after that at my next cleaning Dr. Harman told me I needed to treat my cavity. 6 months later I got a cleaning at a new dentist and they had no mention of a cavity. 6 months after that I got another cleaning from a different dentist and no mention of a cavity. The bottom line was I had no cavity. This can be taken as an honest mistake or misdiagnosis but I’ll explain why I think it’s more than that.

A couple weeks ago my wife’s crown fell out. She has continued to see Dr. Harman who might I add has re-cemented her crown multiple times with it continuing to fall out but this time she was told her tooth was infected and she needed an implant for $9,000. We decided to get a 2nd opinion and the new dentist explained there was zero infection. Now we have 2 conflicting diagnoses so we decided to see a 3rd dentist who also sa
Most disorganized practice ever. Rude office manager completely dropped the ball in transferring from partner practice. Find another practice at all cost.
Totally overcharged me!!!! I won’t go back EVER!!!!!

I was in here months ago but the experience still bothers me to this day. The $300 retainers they had cast clearly did not fit my teeth when I came back into the office weeks later for the try-on. The dentist spent several minutes trying to force the retainers on, to the point of uncomfort and pain. I asked him to stop and asked if it was possible to have another mold taken. Instead of understanding my concern for the clearly wrong fit (I've had retainers before- I know they are supposed to fit on your teeth!) he was taken aback and asked if I think he can't do his job. I was shocked at his instant defensiveness and unprofessionalism. I told him they weren't done correctly and he told me to find someone else.
This dentist is unprofessional, overcharges, and mediocre in ability.

When I made a new patient appt, I told them I had insurance, and that I had an infection, and that I needed a new dentist. They made me wait 3 weeks. Strike 1. When I arrived at the appt, there was a man that stated he had a cracked tooth and had an emergency appt. (He got in within 48 hours, but I had to wait 3 weeks in pain.) Strike 2. Then I'm told they're going to do full mouth X-rays, even though it hurts like * to bite down. They said they couldn't do an eval without full mouth X-rays. Not an X-ray of the impacted broken tooth, but full mouth X-rays. LOL Strike 3. And I said, "then we're done here," and I walked out. I walked out because, by their actions, they've proven to me that they weigh their profits far, far above their patients' welfare. I suggest you go elsewhere too.

Answer to your query: Its definitely you. I'm not giving you my name on the wide open Internet. Ask your people about the woman who walked out.

This is a good dentist but I cancelled my appointment. None of the staff are wearing masks and with the resurgence of COVID with the Omnicron varient… this is totally unacceptable especially in a medical setting. Go at your own risk.
They’re to rude here! Seemed nice, up until the point of filling the forms out.

I recently had some fillings done and now I’m too scared to ever have any more dental work done.

Not only am I still having pain when I eat, but the numbing wore off while my fillings were being done. I let them know when it happened and the first time they injected more lidocaine. The second time I noticed it wore off, they did not give me anything more to numb it and pressured me into just simply finishing. It was one of the worst pains of my life to only create a new problem.

Polite staff, nice office. I’m not one to leave reviews often however, I feel others should be made aware, the reason for my 2 star review is that I had been going to a different dentist for about 12 years, I switched to this office because they no longer accepted the insurance that I had and because it is very close to my work and they have evening availability. When I had my first appointment with the office it had been around a year since my previous cleaning, and Dr. Jason did say that I had 4 teeth that needed fillings. I went ahead and scheduled them to be done. I was also pushed to get retainers and remove my permanent ones. Which I was interested in doing, however it felt a little pushy being the first appointment. Maybe that’s just my opinion.

Now, the second time going to the office it was my routine 6 month visit and again I was told I had 3 cavities. He did show me where the areas were that needed fillings and said there was some stickiness and the teeth were not smooth but honestly I didn’t see what he was referring to and at the end of my visit he said “maybe just eating a lot of sweets?” This is when I became skeptical because I have NEVER in my life had this
This office is horrible! The office manager is rude and has no business in customer service.

Initially, my fiancée and I saw the great reviews and thought this would be the perfect place for us after moving to the area. I can now say, after multiple visits from both of us, that coming here may be a big regret for you.

The biggest issue we ran into was in regards to cavities. I was told I had 4, after living my entire life with none. It was unexpected, for sure, but I figured I may have somehow gotten 4 in the span of the few months since I last visited my previous dentist. They were about $45 each, after insurance. However, I soon realized this was not the case.

My fiancée was told she had multiple cavities, and we spent over $1000 to fill them, after insurance. She comes back a few months later and is told she has 12 more cavities, including on the same teeth that had just been filled prior! It was going to be another almost $750 after insurance to fill them, a little over $60 per filling (why was this now 18% higher?). At this point, we knew something was up. After getting a second opinion from another dentist, we're relieved to know she has TWO cavities, not 12. The blatant lying and overcharging here is beyond ridiculous.
